title: Contact and Ghost
premise: Odile Eastwick, a crash investigator who lost his wife and daughter in an unexplained accident in row twelve, has spent six years buried in cases the powerful want forgotten. When a burner phone arrives containing a voice he knows intimately—his dead wife's—he is pulled into a conspiracy linking that crash to a Russian defector named Anya Volkova, whose extraction Odile is blackmailed into leading. As Odile uncovers that his own agency orchestrated row twelve to silence a witness, and that Anya may be bait to flush out remaining leaks, he must choose between obeying duty one last time or burning his carefully invisible life down. In the end, Odile fakes Anya's death, exposes the agency's director with her evidence, and accepts that the voice on the phone was a synthetic lure—but the found family he builds with Anya and his estranged brother gives him a reason to stop hiding.
about_author: Jonah Oyelaran is a former aviation safety analyst from Lagos who now writes thrillers from a farmhouse outside Porto. His work draws on years spent reading black-box transcripts, and on a lifelong fascination with the lies institutions tell to survive.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Odile works a routine 'attributed' case—a small plane fire ruled accidental despite impossible burn patterns. Flashbacks establish his grief and his reputation for making inconvenient findings disappear quietly. Emotional beat: hollow competence; a man performing normalcy while dead inside.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A padded envelope arrives with no return address: a burner phone that rings. The voice is his wife Marion's, reciting details of row twelve only she could know—and one detail she never knew: a second passenger manifest. Odile traces the phone to a dead drop and finds a photo of defector Anya Volkova. Emotional beat: terror and hunger; grief weaponized into hope.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, with a cold interlude from Director Hale's perspective. Agency fixer Merrick confronts Odile: take the extraction job or lose what's left of his clearance and protection. Hale's chapter reveals the agency fears what Anya carries. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as choice; Odile realizes 'invisible' was always someone else's permission.

chapters.title: The Defector
chapters.summary: Anya's POV introduced. Hiding in Tallinn under three names, Anya tests her new handler by feeding him a lie—and watches it travel up the chain exactly as predicted, confirming she's being used as bait. She decides to run her own game. Emotional beat: wary intelligence; two hunted people circling the same trap from opposite sides.

chapters.title: Extraction Protocol
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The extraction begins badly: safehouse burned, team compromised, and Odile realizes the leak came from inside the op. He and Anya escape together through the port district, and she reveals she knew Marion—the crash wasn't random. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to a fragile, unwilling alliance.

chapters.title: What Anya Knew
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Odile and Anya in a farmhouse safehouse. Anya explains: row twelve held a whistleblower carrying proof of a sanctioned arms pipeline; the agency shot the plane down. The voice on the burner is a deepfake built from Marion's recovered voicemails—bait calibrated to Odile specifically. Emotional beat: devastation; hope curdling, then hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Long Con
chapters.summary: Anya's POV. Instead of running, they decide to let the agency believe the extraction succeeded. Anya coaches Odile through playing the loyal asset while she forges a duplicate of her evidence cache. A quiet scene where Odile almost breaks watching a fake message from 'Marion.' Emotional beat: found family forming under fire; trust chosen, not given.

chapters.title: Brother's Keeper
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile recruits his estranged brother Tomas, a disgraced journalist, to hold the evidence dead-man-switch style. Merrick closes in, forcing Odile to feed him a flawless performance. Hale orders the op terminated—with prejudice. Emotional beat: reconciliation and dread; the family Odile rebuilt is now on the kill list too.

chapters.title: The Handoff
chapters.summary: Odile and Anya's alternating POV. Climax at a decommissioned airfield: the staged handoff becomes an ambush. Merrick turns on Hale's order, Odile turns the agency's own surveillance net against them, broadcasting Anya's evidence mid-firefight. Merrick dies; Hale escapes wounded. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal—Odile chooses the person over the institution, at gunpoint.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, epilogue months later. The evidence detonates publicly; Hale is arrested, though the machine grinds on. The burner rings one last time—Odile lets it ring out and buries it beside row twelve's memorial. He, Anya, and Tomas gather for a plain dinner, unremarkable and alive. Emotional beat: grief integrated, not erased; visibility chosen at last.
